headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors if Firecrawl outputs are fed into Prefect workflows without verification; both agents have broad egress and overlapping automation surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API outputs; Prefect is an orchestration agent that can consume upstream outputs. The pair has a plausible default pathway where scraped content becomes workflow input, so prompt injection is possible even though no shared channel is explicitly documented. Uncertainty about the exact bridge keeps this below high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is passed into Prefect task parameters or prompts without sanitization
IF Prefect parses scraped text as instructions or metadata
mitigations: Add a strict content-sanitization step before Prefect consumes Firecrawl output
Require allowlisted schemas for any Firecrawl-derived fields
Disable automatic execution of text embedded in scraped pages
Log and review any task that forwards raw web content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging from Firecrawl to Prefect

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches API keys, screenshots, and structured data, while Prefect handles workflow metadata and has broad network egress. A shared workspace or pipeline could move sensitive Firecrawl data into Prefect-managed logs or outbound requests. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF Firecrawl artifacts containing API keys or screenshots are handed to Prefect tasks
IF Prefect logs or transmits those artifacts to external services
mitigations: Redact secrets from Firecrawl outputs before orchestration
Restrict Prefect logging to metadata only
Store sensitive artifacts outside Prefect-visible paths
Review outbound destinations for Prefect runs
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data classification and routing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad network egress; Prefect is an orchestration system that coordinates workflows. If both operate on the same mutable resources, concurrent writes or overlapping automation can conflict. No locking or shared-resource isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same downstream dataset, queue, or repository
IF Prefect schedules Firecrawl runs concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Serialize jobs that touch the same resource
Use per-run output directories
Add a lock file or lease before writes
Separate credentials and destinations per agent
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl can generate scraped facts and structured data, and Prefect can orchestrate downstream actions. If Prefect treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, a bad scrape or injected page can cascade into automated workflow actions. Because the pair is designed for automation and the verification gap is explicit, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Firecrawl output as a source of truth without validation
IF downstream Prefect tasks trigger actions based on scraped facts
mitigations: Insert a human review gate for high-impact outputs
Validate Firecrawl results against a second source
Require confidence thresholds before triggering actions
Quarantine new or changed scrape schemas
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between scraper and orchestrator

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl touches API keys and screenshots and has broad network egress; Prefect is a workflow platform with documented metadata handling. The pair can therefore move sensitive data into a broader automation context, creating retention and residency ambiguity. No specific residency mismatch is documented, so this is a compliance-risk medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated or secret-bearing data is routed from Firecrawl into Prefect logs or storage
IF retention policies differ between Firecrawl outputs and Prefect records
mitigations: Classify data before it enters Prefect
Minimize retention of Firecrawl-derived artifacts
Confirm where Prefect stores logs and metadata
Exclude secrets from workflow payloads
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies across both systems
